pricing.note: Every unpaid call answers HTTP 402 with the canonical x402 challenge; the amount in that response is the price. No free tier, no signup, no API keys.

tools.description: Read-only operation — no side effects, no parameters. Returns the live Base market snapshot: aggregated activity, daily request/sales counters, the official agent catalog, and real-time market data (CoinGecko, DEXScreener, Fear & Greed). Use it for market context and price/indicator lookups; use get_onchain_sales for paid-call revenue and get_bot_status for integration health..

tools.description: Read-only operation — no side effects, no parameters. Returns the real on-chain payment history to this service's fee receiver on Base: total_volume_usd, total_sales, by_token, up to 100 history rows (tx hash, payer, amount, block, timestamp), source="real_blockchain", plus the wallet state and a market snapshot. Use it when you need provable revenue or settlement evidence; use get_market_stats for prices and get_bot_status for integration health..

tools.description: Read-only operation — no side effects, no parameters. Returns the service's Telegram integration status as JSON: telegram_bot_running, telegram_token_configured, last_heartbeat, uptime_started, messages_sent, active_users, commands_processed, vip_invites_sent, plus the wallet state. Use it to confirm this service's own monitoring is alive (and its heartbeat recent) before trusting other outputs; use get_market_stats for market data or get_onchain_sales for provable revenue..
tools.name: get_bot_status

tools.description: Read-only operation — no side effects, no parameters. Returns this service's flagship trading-agent signals for ETH, ONDO, KAITO and DEGEN: action, confidence, price_usd and the model's reasoning. Use it when you need a directional call rather than raw market data; use get_whale_flow for large-transfer flow and get_arbitrage_opportunities for cross-DEX spreads..
tools.name: get_trading_signal

tools.description: Read-only operation — no side effects, no parameters. Returns network-wide USDC whale flow on Base: transfers of $5M or more, refreshed every 60 seconds, with labelled counterparties. Use it to see where size is moving; use get_trading_signal for directional calls or get_market_stats for broad context..
tools.name: get_whale_flow

tools.description: Read-only operation — no side effects, no parameters. Returns live cross-DEX arbitrage spreads on Base, refreshed every 60 seconds. Use it for executable price gaps between venues; use get_market_stats for aggregate prices or get_trading_signal for directional calls..
tools.name: get_arbitrage_opportunities

server.name: io.github.hu-chenyu/log-ai-compressor
server.description: Local log forensics: compress logs into citable evidence with root-cause confidence tiers.
server.title: log-ai-compressor

benchmark.note: Measured on 10 Loghub-2.0 datasets (ISSTA'24) whose event templates are human-annotated. At an equal 32k-token budget, evidence retention vs Drain3 is 7 wins / 1 tie / 2 losses - the two losses (HPC, Mac) are documented with root causes rather than hidden. Output size stays bounded in the low hundreds of tokens regardless of log size (re-measured 313-788 tokens on 120k-180k line logs), whereas Drain3's output grows from 317 to 566,802 tokens. Full methodology and limitations: https://github.com/hu-chenyu/log-ai-compressor/blob/main/docs/BENCHMARK.md

privacy.note: All analysis runs on-device. The server only reads local file paths the calling agent passes in; no network calls are made unless the optional AI-interpretation layer is explicitly configured.

tools.description: Analyze one or more local log files (merged oldest-first by mtime, suitable for rotated logs). Returns error clusters ranked by priority, each with a root-cause confidence tier (CONFIRMED / LIKELY / INSUFFICIENT) and an explicit list of what evidence is still missing. Runs fully on-device.
tools.name: analyze_log_file

tools.description: Analyze a log text directly — pasted content, command output, or a fragment an agent already read. Same clustering and root-cause confidence output, without touching the filesystem.
tools.name: analyze_log_text

tools.description: Compare 2-5 log files and list errors that are new, disappeared, or common relative to a baseline file. Answers 'what changed between this deploy and the last one'.
tools.name: compare_log_files

tools.description: Export analysis as a compressed report in md / json / text / html / summary format. Markdown and summary are tuned for pasting into an LLM: a few hundred tokens instead of millions of raw log lines, with every finding still carrying its line numbers for citation.
tools.name: export_report

tools.description: Retrieve the full evidence for one error cluster: representative raw log line, surrounding context lines, de-noised stack trace, instance line-number index, and the reasoning behind its root-cause verdict.
tools.name: get_cluster_detail

tools.description: List built-in log parsing rule templates and the log formats each targets. Check this first when a log parses badly.
tools.name: list_rules

tools.description: Re-read the source log and re-verify every evidence reference in a report: file, line range, sha256 digest. Returns one of four verdicts - VERIFIED (every reference matches), TAMPERED (content really changed), UNVERIFIABLE (cannot check right now, e.g. the log is momentarily locked by another process - NOT an accusation of tampering), NO_EVIDENCE. This is the tool's trust anchor - the agent does not need to believe the analysis, it can re-run this step itself.
tools.name: verify_evidence

tools.description: Self-check with no arguments: confirms the tool is importable and reports version, available built-in rules, and whether optional AI interpretation is configured.
tools.name: check_environment
